title: How can we check divisibility without long division?
description: Forty eight is divisible by twelve, and the rows of primes show why. The primes of twelve sit inside the primes of forty eight. Keeko doubts this and says sharing some primes is enough.
teaching_notes: One idea: a number is divisible by another when the primes of the other are all included in its own primes. Watch for students who think sharing some primes is enough.

source: We say that 48 is divisible by 12 because when we divide 48
video_script.why: The child sees that divisibility can be checked by looking for the primes of the divisor inside the primes of the number.
video_script.substitution: the book's own numbers, forty eight and twelve
video_script.anchor: the rows of primes of forty eight and twelve, with the row of twelve ringed inside the row of forty eight
video_script.wrong_answer: sharing some primes is enough for one number to divide the other
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko sees that forty eight and twelve share the primes two and three, and thinks any shared primes mean divisibility.
video_script.payoff_line: A number is divisible by another when the primes of the other are all included in its primes

final_answer.value: A number is divisible by another when the prime factorisation of the other is included in its own; 48 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 includes 12 = 2 × 2 × 3
final_answer.spoken: check whether the primes of the divisor are included in the primes of the number

maths_rules: the row 2 × 2 × 3 of 12 is found inside the row of 48, leaving two 2s
10 = 2 × 5 and 15 = 3 × 5 share the prime 5, but neither divides the other
video_script.design: The rows of primes of forty eight and twelve are written one above the other. The primes of twelve are ringed inside the row of forty eight, and the leftover primes make the other factor.

<bookmark mark='div'/>When we divide forty eight by twelve, the remainder is zero, so forty eight is divisible by twelve.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How can we check this without long division?

narration: <bookmark mark='mult'/>Step three, check. The ringed primes make twelve, and the two twos make four, so forty eight is twelve times four.

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>A number is divisible by another when the primes of the other are all included in its primes.
